editorial:
Imagine moving to a new city for college and finding a place that feels like a second home. That is exactly what happens to Lena and Benhur when they move from Jakarta to Malang. Their new boarding house seems perfect, with friendly owners and weekly dinners where everyone hangs out. The vibe is warm and cozy at first, but things get creepy fast. When one of the students starts talking about a scary dream and a ghost wrapped in a white shroud, you might think it is just a prank. But once Lena sees the ghost for herself, the mood shifts from a college dream to a total nightmare. You will feel the tension build as you realize the house is hiding a dark secret.

What really makes this work is how the scary moments hit you out of nowhere. The acting feels real, and the pacing keeps you on edge without feeling too slow. While some of the jump scares are a bit predictable, the twist about the cost of living there is a great shock. If you love scary movies with a big reveal, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the owners are not just landlords, but cult leaders. They use the boarding house to lure in young students to sacrifice them to a demon to keep their own youth and power. In the end, Lena manages to fight back and escape, but Benhur is trapped. The movie closes with the chilling realization that the cycle will just start again with a new set of students moving in.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural horror and twist endings.
